content:
alice: FYI customer acme-inc on dedicated pool eu-prod-3 is seeing steady 429s during short bursts. They claim they're within committed QPS (200). Ticket: #INC-12345
ben_sre: When did it start?
alice: ~14:03 UTC, spikes every 10-15s for ~30s windows. Latency also climbs from 45ms to 800ms
chandra_support: Can you paste the auth header they use and the pool id?
alice: header masked: `Authorization: Bearer ****` pool: `eu-prod-3-reserved-1`
chandra_support: Running quick check — can you share `x-dedicated-token-usage` from response headers when they get 429?
alice: grabbing, attaching snippet:
```
x-dedicated-token-usage: reserved=180/200;window=30s;burst=20
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
```
ben_sre: Hmm reserved=180/200 but burst=20 — that should allow short overshoot. Are they hitting per-route token limits or global qps guard?
dana_platform: Also check if there was a rapid model fallback or cold-start causing queueing. Any recent rollouts?
deploy-bot: deployment: redwood/runtime v3.9.2 to eu-prod completed 2026-03-17T13:58:10Z
chandra_support: Good call — if throughput cap enforced before burst smoothing kicks in, requests pile. Can you run a repro with `ab` or `hey` at 220 qps for 40s and capture `x-rate-window`?
alice: running now, sending results in a sec
alice: repro run attached:
```
> hey -z 40s -q 220 -c 50 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
responses: 429 @ ~6s, then sustained 429s ~6-36s
header sample:
x-rate-window: 30s
x-dedicated-token-usage: reserved=185/200;window=30s;burst=20
x-rate-smoothing: active
```
ben_sre: So the rate-smoothing header is active but burst isn't preventing 429s — could be token refill granularity or auth shard mismatch
chandra_support: Ask customer for client-side retry/jitter? But we should surface to infra. @dana_platform can you verify token-bucket refill config on eu-prod-3? Might be set to 1s ticks and penalty window interfering
dana_platform: digging into config — eu-prod-3 reserved pool is `commit=200 qps;burst=25;penalty=30s;refill_ms=500`. I see an oddness: refill_ms honored on a per-worker basis; when busy we observed effective refill slower
ben_sre: That could explain queue buildup if worker count decreased during rollout. Any autoscale events at that time?
dana_platform: Autoscaler had two pods drain for rolling update at 13:57-13:59, reducing workers by ~30% briefly
chandra_support: That timing aligns with deploy-bot timestamp. So during drain the effective refill capacity drops -> bursts can't be absorbed -> 429s
alice: Customer reported they didn't see increased retries; they hit 429 and surface error to end-users. They want SLA alignment explanation
chandra_support: Proposed remediation: 1) immediate: increase burst allowance on pool to 35 for eu-prod-3, 2) short-term: adjust autoscaler to keep min-workers at current committed headroom during deploys, 3) long-term: move smoothing to be global per-pool rather than per-worker
ben_sre: For the immediate patch I'll open infra ticket to bump burst to 35 for that pool and add sticky warm capacity during rollouts
chandra_support: Also send customer remediation steps: exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency where possible; we can offer temporary dedicated extra headroom for 24h
billing-bot: Note: temporary headroom on reserved pools may incur additional billing; will share authorization flow
alice: I'll send customer update and attach repro logs + suggested retry snippet:
```
# client retry example
for attempt in range(5):
  resp = call_api()
  if resp.status_code==429:
    sleep((2**attempt)/10 + random.uniform(0,0.1))
  else: break
```
dana_platform: I'm filing INFRA-7899 to track config drift and rollout-safe autoscale
chandra_support: thanks. Marking thread resolved once infra confirms burst bump and we share note with customer
alice: thanks all :thumbsup:
